corpusSummary: Across 2026, social-science studies deploy and critique large language models (LLMs) in health, education, policy, and culture. The corpus highlights methodological innovations (LLM-assisted coding, multi-agent simulations, governance frameworks), rising attention to trust, embodiment, and social influence in human–AI interactions, and ongoing concerns about fairness, bias, and safety. Applications span health misinformation, ESG, AI literacy, and heritage preservation, signaling both promise and need for validation.

themes.name: LLM-enabled research methods and governance
themes.description: Papers show LLM-assisted data analysis, coding, simulations, and governance frameworks, emphasizing validation, transparency, and ethical oversight across domains.

themes.name: Trust, embodiment, and social dynamics in human–AI interaction
themes.description: A cross-domain thread examines how perceptions of humanness, AI embodiment, privacy, and social influences shape trust, acceptance, and collaboration with AI.

themes.name: Equity, bias, and representation in AI deployment
themes.description: Studies assess fairness, cultural adequacy, representation, and governance strategies to mitigate disparities in health, education, and policy contexts.

themes.name: Education, learning, and heritage in AI-enabled contexts
themes.description: GenAI applications in education, AI literacy for diverse populations, and heritage-oriented design explore learning gains alongside risks like overreliance and ethics.

emergingKeywords: cultural adequacy and representation in AI
